# Closure and Escalation Notes

**Scheduled Task Created With Suspicious Action** · `T1053.005_schtasks_suspicious_creation` · [T1053.005](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text

Observed:     Image=<value>  OriginalFileName=<value>  CommandLine=<value>
Checked:      1. Validate the host and user -> <result>
              2. Review the task name and action -> <result>
              3. Check whether the action points to a user-writable path -> <result>
              4. Check the parent process -> <result>
              5. Search the same user and host for 30 minutes either side -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | office_click_to_run (proposed) | sccm_client (proposed) | all_powershell_actions (rejected)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- IT automation that schedules PowerShell maintenance scripts
- Office Click-to-Run registering Office's update and telemetry tasks from XML files under C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\ClickToRun

Never tune:
- Never filter remote creation as SYSTEM (/S with /RU SYSTEM): it is a lateral-movement pattern.

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. Remote creation with /S and /RU SYSTEM
2. An existing task's action changed (/change) to a new binary
3. Action runs PowerShell, cmd, mshta, wscript, cscript or regsvr32
4. Payload under AppData, ProgramData, Public or Temp

Risk conditions: remote execution +20 · payload in user writable path +15 · host is critical +15 · suspicious parent +15 · approved admin activity -25 · approved change window -20.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Preserve the task XML before deleting anything
2. Disable the task
3. Isolate the host if the payload executed
4. For remote creation, investigate the source host
